questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 ?
questions.explain: Count the 2s: there are 4 of them, so this is 4 groups of 2, which is 4 × 2 = 8. Counting one group too many gives 5 × 2, which is 2 too much, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 2 × 2 or 5 × 4. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Xin Yi works out 5093 + 2063 in columns. One column makes 15, so she writes 5 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is the 5 she writes there worth?
questions.stemText: Xin Yi works out 5093 + 2063 in columns. One column makes 15, so she writes 5 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is the 5 she writes there worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 15 is the tens column: 9 + 6 = 15, and no other column reaches ten. 15 tens is 1 hundred and 5 tens, so the 5 stays in the tens column - worth 50 - and the small 1 goes above the hundreds column - worth 100. The 5 is worth 50. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stemText: Xin Yi works out 9934 − 3998. In every column she takes the smaller digit away from the bigger one, and gets 6064. What is the correct answer?
